headline: Meridian Energy historically a beneficiary of El Niño through above-average South Island hydro generation, though 2026 cycle dynamics may differ
reasoning: Meridian's predominantly South Island hydro generation profile has historically positioned it as a beneficiary during El Niño periods, which bring above-average hydro inflows to that region. However, the current cycle starts from high lake storage levels across the whole country, and the expanded role of wind, solar and battery storage may alter the traditional dynamics. A material roll-off in wholesale futures prices in recent months may also affect future company profitability.
quote: For the listed gentailers from a generation production perspective this has been beneficial for Meridian and Contact Energy and a modest headwind for Mercury, reflecting their hydro generation locations. However, with the system currently running at relatively full lake levels across the whole country the individual gentailer impact this time around may be different. In the last decade we have also seen substantial investment in other generation including wind, solar and battery storage which will influence the El Niño cycle impact on wholesale prices.
episode_title: Not just a weather event. What does the 2026 El Niño weather event mean for NZ investment markets?

headline: Salt Long Short Fund covered most of its Meridian Energy short after ETF-driven bubble pushed stock up sharply, but warns it will 'crack into an abyss'
reasoning: MEL rose +15.4% in December and a further +15.8% on January 5, driven by massive inflows into two clean energy ETFs benchmarked to the S&P Global Clean Energy Index, where MEL has a ~5.5% weighting. Those ETFs grew from US$2.5bn at the time of Biden's election to US$10.5bn, with passive funds alone now holding ~10% of MEL's free float. The fund views MEL as absurdly expensive on any free cashflow metric and sees this as a classic example of passive becoming too large for the underlying security. The stock is not expected to be rebalanced out of the index until April. The fund covered most of its short on a brief pullback and will be cautious re-entering, but maintains the view that when the bubble breaks, the fall will be severe.
quote: MEL is one of 30 stocks in the S&P Global Clean Energy Index with a weighting of around 5.5%. Two huge clean energy ETF's are benchmarked to this index. At the time of Joe Biden's election, these had assets of US$2.5bn. They grew to US$5.5bn at end-Nov and are now around US$10.5bn as this is written... Never mind that MEL is absurdly expensive on any free cashflow based metric. This is a classic example of passive starting to become too big for the underlying securities that comprise it. MEL will likely be rebalanced down in the index but this is unlikely until April and who knows where it will be by then. We used a fleeting pull-back to cover most of the short and will be rather cautious in trying again. However, when it cracks, it will crack into an abyss.
